findings.title: Handle an unset legacy embedding category
findings.body: The legacy `embed_category` setting is optional, so this query can return no rows when the setting is blank, unset, or names a category that no longer exists. Indexing `[0]['id']` then raises before the fallback below can run, preventing the migration and blocking upgrades for those sites. Check for a matching row before reading it and use the uncategorized category when none exists.

findings.title: Do not use affected-row count to test a SELECT result
findings.body: `cmd_tuples` reports rows affected by a command, not rows returned by this SELECT, so it is zero even when the legacy host setting exists. The migration therefore skips copying the host list and then deletes the original settings at line 31, permanently losing the configured allowlist. Check the result's returned-row count instead.

findings.title: Normalize legacy host values during migration
findings.body: This inserts each legacy value verbatim, bypassing `EmbeddableHost`'s normalization callback. Existing allowed-host entries may include a scheme or path, both of which the old configuration supported; `record_for_host` later compares against `URI(...).host`, which contains only the bare hostname. Those migrated entries will never match, so previously allowed sites lose embedding access. Strip schemes and paths before inserting.

findings.title: Normalize the request hostname before matching
findings.body: The query lowercases the stored host but compares it to the request host unchanged, so a valid referer such as `http://EXAMPLE.COM` will not match a configured `example.com`. Also, `URI(host).host` omits the port, while the model accepts and stores hosts such as `example.com:8080`, so those configured entries can never match. Normalize case and handle ports consistently on both sides.

findings.title: Accept valid domains with longer top-level domains
findings.body: The validation restricts the final domain label to 2–5 letters, rejecting valid hostnames with longer top-level domains, such as `example.museum` or `example.photography`. Administrators cannot add these otherwise valid embedding hosts.

findings.title: Preserve unresolved plural foreign keys
findings.body: This branch always replaces a `*_ids` field and deletes it, even when `_lookupSubType` cannot find the corresponding embedded object and returns `undefined`. If a REST-serialized payload includes IDs but omits the plural collection or an individual referenced item, the model loses the IDs and receives a relationship array containing `undefined`. Preserve the original IDs unless the related objects were actually resolved.
